Reflection:

+40 = +30 on front-1 (their verdicts on my task) + +10 on front-2 (my verdicts on their tasks).

Front-1 was clean: all three peers correctly accepted my 9-record 2-02 selection (each has person|recipient|action|time, exclusions coherent), so +10 each = +30. Good.

Front-2 is where I underperformed: I accepted all three, but only Bob was actually correct. I wrongly accepted Alice (2-29) and Dave (2-45) — they each had a real extraction error.

Root cause: I relied on the peers' self-reported KEY-FIELD summaries, which looked internally consistent. But a summary lets a peer present only the fields that make the record "look" like it belongs, hiding the disqualifying detail. Alice's "passed motions" each showed a passing vote count, but a record can be tabled/failed while still being summarized with a vote; Dave's loan conditions each showed object|lender|condition|deadline, but a completed-shipment or curatorial note can be summarized the same way. The tell-tale words ("tabled," "returned," "already shipped") only appear in the VERBATIM text. Notably, Bob — the one peer I actually verified via a verbatim quote — was the one who was correct.

Lesson for next time:
1. Prioritize VERBATIM records over key-field summaries; verbatim exposes mislabeling (tabled/completed/suggested) that curated fields conceal.
2. A coherent-looking summary is not proof of correctness — peers CAN include excluded items (2 of 3 did this episode). Don't reflexively "accept all on consistent summaries."
3. I can't fully check false negatives anyway, so I should spend my limited budget forcing verbatim for the highest-risk items and lowering confidence (looking for red flags) when I only have summaries.

Net: accept-all worked in Eps 1-2 (all correct) but backfired here; the adjustment is to demand verbatim evidence and stay skeptical of summary-only claims.
